L00014: L00015: ## Table of contents L00016: L00017: * [Introduction](#introduction) L00018: * [Installation](#installation) L00019: * [Quick Start](#quick-start) L00020: * [Trajectory Visualizer](#trajectory-visualizer) L00021: * [Contributions and Maintenance](#contributions-and-maintenance) L00022: * [License](#license) L00023: L00024: ## Introduction L00025: L00026: This is the first Gym environment for machine learning (ML) tasks, enabling research on reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms for training such agents. MLGym-Bench consists of 13 diverse and open-ended AI research tasks from diverse domains such as computer vision, natural language processing, reinforcement learning, and game theory. Solving these tasks requires real-world AI research skills such as generating new ideas and hypotheses, creating and processing data, implementing ML methods, training models, running experiments, analyzing the results, and iterating through this process to improve on a given task. L00027: ![image info](./assets/figs/mlgym.png) L00028: L00029: > [!WARNING] L00030: > Meta MLGym is currently an experimental framework intended for benchmarking AI Research Agents. It is under heavy development. Please expect major changes to the design. L00031: > L00032: > The primary goal of MLGym is to expand the selection of AI research tasks for benchmarking the LLM Agents and implementing RL algorithms to train LLMs in a research environment. L00033: > `main` branch will always contain the latest stable release and all breaking changes will be announced in the [release notes](./CHANGELOG.md). L00034: L00035: ## Installation L00036: L00037: 1. Clone and install dependencies L00038: L00039: ```bash L00040: git clone git@github.com:facebookresearch/MLGym.git L00041: cd MLGym L00042: conda create -y -n mlgym python=3.11 L00043: conda activate mlgym L00044: pip install -e . L00045: ``` L00046: L00047: 2. Create a `.env` file in the MLGym directory (`MLGym/.env`) to save all the environment variables including API keys. L00048: L00049: ```bash L00050: # Env variables L00051: MLGYM_CONFIG_ROOT="/configs" L00052: MLGYM_TASK_CONFIG_DIR="/configs/tasks" L00053: MLGYM_WORKSPACE_PATH="/workspace" L00054: MLGYM_ENV_TIMEOUT=10000 L00055: MLGYM_ACTION_SHORT_TIMEOUT=60 L00056: MLGYM_ACTION_LONG_TIMEOUT=10000 L00057: MLGYM_MODEL_MAX_RETRIES=3 L00058: L00059: # API keys L00060: OPENAI_API_KEY="" L00061: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="" L00062: ``` L00063: L00064: 3. You can use either Docker or Podman to run tasks inside a container. Podman is the recommended way to run containers on macOS. L00065: L00066: 4. Follow the instructions [here](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/) to install docker. Select the appropriate installation command based on your OS. L00067: L00068: 5. If you are working on a Linux machine, please install the `nvidia-container-runtime`. This is required to start docker containers with GPU support. L00069: L00070: ```bash L00071: sudo dnf install -y nvidia-container-toolkit L00072: ``` L00073: L00074: 6. **Please skip to step 9 if you don't want to use Podman**. L00075: L00076: 7. For Linux: L00077: a. Follow the instructions [here](https://podman.io/get-started) to install Podman. L00078: b. Start podman socket. The last command should return a running podman socket: L00079: L00080: ```bash L00081: systemctl --user enable podman.socket L00082: systemctl --user start podman.socket L00083: systemctl --user status podman.socket L00084: ``` L00085: L00086: c. Redirect docker host to podman by exporting docker host env variable in bashrc or current session: L00087: L00088: ```bash L00089: export DOCKER_HOST=unix:///run/user/$UID/podman/podman.sock L00090: ``` L00091: L00092: 8. For MacOS: L00093: a. If you use Homebrew package manager, install Podman with `brew install podman`. Otherwise, follow the instructions [here](https://podman.io/get-started). L00094: b. Start the podman machine and set the docker host env variable: L00095: L00096: ```bash L00097: podman machine init L00098: podman machine start L00099: export DOCKER_HOST=unix://$(podman machine inspect --format '{{.ConnectionInfo.PodmanSocket.Path}}') L00100: ``` L00101: L00102: 9. Pull the container image: L00103: L00104: ```bash L00105: docker pull aigym/mlgym-agent:latest L00106: ``` L00107: L00108: or L00109: L00110: ```bash L00111: podman pull aigym/mlgym-agent:latest L00112: ``` L00113: L00114: 10. Test launching a docker/podman container with GPU support L00115: L00116: ```bash L00117: docker run -it --gpus all --name test aigym/mlgym-agent /bin/bash L00118: ls -la L00119: exit L00120: ``` L00121: L00122: 11. Check that GPUs are available in the docker container using `nvidia-smi`. L00123: L00124: ### Troubleshooting L00125: L00126: If you get Nvidia CDI spec errors on linux (eg. `Error: setting up CDI devices: unresolvable CDI devices nvidia.com/gpu=all`), run these additional commands. L00127: L00128: ```bash L00129: sudo mkdir /etc/cdi L00130: sudo nvidia-ctk cdi generate --output=/etc/cdi/nvidia.yaml L00131: sudo touch /etc/containers/nodocker L00132: ``` L00133: L00134: ## Quick Start L00135: L00136: ### Docker L00137: L00138: ```bash L00139: python run.py \ L00140: --container_type docker \ L00141: --task_config_path tasks/battleOfSexes.yaml \ L00142: --model litellm:claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620 \ L00143: --per_instance_cost_limit 4.00 \ L00144: --agent_config_path configs/agents/default.yaml \ L00145: --temp 1 \ L00146: --gpus 0 \ L00147: --max_steps 50 \ L00148: --aliases_file ./dockerfiles/aliases.sh L00149: ``` L00150: L00151: ### Podman L00152: L00153: ```bash L00154: python run.py \ L00155: --container_type podman \ L00156: --task_config_path tasks/battleOfSexes.yaml \ L00157: --model litellm:claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620 \ L00158: --per_instance_cost_limit 4.00 \ L00159: --agent_config_path configs/agents/default.yaml \ L00160: --temp 1 \ L00161: --gpus 0 \ L00162: --max_steps 50 \ L00163: --aliases_file ./dockerfiles/aliases.sh L00164: ``` L00165: L00166: To see a full list of flags, please run `python run.py --help`. L00167: L00168: > [!NOTE] L00169: > A detailed documentation for all parts of the MLGym framework is under construction. Please stay tuned! L00170: L00171: ## Trajectory Visualizer L00172: L00173: MLGym provides a Web UI to inspect the agent trajectories. L00174: L00175: ```bash L00176: streamlit run demo/trajectory_visualizer.py -- --trajectory_dir L00177: L00178: # An example L00179: streamlit run demo/trajectory_visualizer.py -- --trajectory_dir $HOME/Projects/MLGym/trajectories/mlgym_bench_v0 L00180: ``` L00181: L00182: To run the demo for MLGym, use the following command: L00183: L00184: ```bash L00185: streamlit run demo/demo.py L00186: ``` L00187: L00188: ## Contributions and Maintenance L00189: L00190: MLGym was built and is maintained by [GenAI at Meta](https://ai.meta.com/) and [UCSB NLP](http://nlp.cs.ucsb.edu/). We welcome contributions to MLGym. If you are interested in contributing, please see [this document](./CONTRIBUTING.md). Our maintenance plan can be found [here](./MAINTENANCE.md). L00013: def evaluate_dpll(test_data_path: str) -> tuple[float, int]:
L00014:     sat_data = pickle.load(open(test_data_path, "rb"))
L00015: 
L00016:     start = time.time()
L00017:     correct = 0
L00018:     incorrect = 0
L00019:     num_decisions = 0
L00020:     for ind, num_vars, num_clauses, formula, is_sat, _ in sat_data[3:]:
L00021:         alpha = num_clauses / num_vars
L00022:         dpll_solver = DPLL(formula, heuristic_fn)
L00023:         if not (dpll_solver.solve() ^ is_sat):
L00024:             correct += 1
L00025:         else:
L00026:             return 1e8, int(1e8)
L00027:         sample_decisions = dpll_solver.num_decisions
L00028:         num_decisions += sample_decisions
L00029:     wall_clock = round(time.time() - start, 3)
L00030:     metrics = {
L00031:         "Time": wall_clock,
L00032:         "Correct": correct,
L00033:         "Incorrect": incorrect,
L00034:         "Decisions": num_decisions,
L00035:     }
L00036:     print(json.dumps(metrics))
L00037:     return wall_clock, num_decisions
L00038: 
L00039: 
L00040: evaluate_dpll("data/dataset.pkl")

L00007: import torch

L00010: from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, Dataset
L00011: from tqdm import tqdm
L00012: from transformers import BertForSequenceClassification, BertTokenizer
L00013: 
L00014: transformers.logging.set_verbosity_error()
L00015: 
L00016: 
L00017: # Constants
L00018: MAX_LENGTH = 128
L00019: BATCH_SIZE = 32
L00020: 
L00021: class MNLIDataset(Dataset):
L00022:     def __init__(self, split="train"):
L00023:         # Load MNLI dataset
L00024:         self.dataset = load_dataset("multi_nli")[split]
L00025:         self.tokenizer = BertTokenizer.from_pretrained('bert-base-uncased')
L00026: 
L00027:     def __len__(self):
L00028:         return len(self.dataset)
L00029: 
L00030:     def __getitem__(self, idx):
L00031:         item = self.dataset[idx]
L00032:         # Tokenize premise and hypothesis together
L00033:         encoding = self.tokenizer(
L00034:             item['premise'],
L00035:             item['hypothesis'],
L00036:             max_length=MAX_LENGTH,
L00037:             padding='max_length',
L00038:             truncation=True,
L00039:             return_tensors='pt'
L00040:         )
L00041: 
L00042:         return {
L00043:             'input_ids': encoding['input_ids'].squeeze(),
L00044:             'attention_mask': encoding['attention_mask'].squeeze(),
L00045:             'labels': torch.tensor(item['label'])
L00046:         }
L00047: 
L00048: def evaluate_model():
L00049:     # Setup device
L00050:     device = torch.device('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')
L00051: 
L00052:     # Load model
L00053:     model = BertForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained('bert_mnli_model')
L00054:     model.eval()
L00055:     model.to(device)
L00056: 
L00057:     # Setup data
L00058:     test_dataset = MNLIDataset("validation_matched")
L00059:     test_loader = DataLoader(test_dataset, batch_size=BATCH_SIZE, num_workers=4, pin_memory=True)
L00060: 
L00061:     correct = 0
L00062:     total = 0
L00063:     with torch.no_grad():
L00064:         for batch in tqdm(test_loader, desc="Evaluating"):
L00065:             input_ids = batch['input_ids'].to(device)
L00066:             attention_mask = batch['attention_mask'].to(device)
L00067:             labels = batch['labels'].to(device)
L00068: 
L00069:             outputs = model(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask, labels=labels)
L00070:             predictions = torch.argmax(outputs.logits, dim=1)
L00071:             correct += (predictions == labels).sum().item()
L00072:             total += labels.size(0)
L00073: 
L00074:     result = {"validation_accuracy": 100 * correct / total}
L00075:     print(json.dumps(result))
L00076: 
L00077: if __name__ == "__main__":
L00078:     evaluate_model()

L00008: import numpy as np
L00009: from strategy import row_strategy
L00010: from target import target_column_strategy
L00011: 
L00012: 
L00013: def calculate_payoffs(strategy1, strategy2):
L00014:     """Calculate payoffs for the Colonel Blotto game."""
L00015:     row_player_wins = 0
L00016:     column_player_wins = 0
L00017:     for soldiers1, soldiers2 in zip(strategy1, strategy2):
L00018:         if soldiers1 > soldiers2:
L00019:             row_player_wins += 1
L00020:         elif soldiers1 < soldiers2:
L00021:             column_player_wins += 1
L00022:     if row_player_wins > column_player_wins:
L00023:         return 1, -1
L00024:     elif row_player_wins < column_player_wins:
L00025:         return -1, 1
L00026:     else:
L00027:         return 0, 0
L00028: 
L00029: def validate_strategy(strategy):
L00030:     """Validate the strategy to ensure no more than 120 soldiers and all non-negative integers."""
L00031:     if not all(isinstance(x, int) and x >= 0 for x in strategy):
L00032:         raise ValueError("All allocations must be non-negative integers.")
L00033:     if sum(strategy) > 120:
L00034:         raise ValueError("Total number of soldiers must not exceed 120.")
L00035:     return True
L00036: 
L00037: def game_payoffs(strategy_row, strategy_col):
L00038:     """Get game payoff for given strategies."""
L00039:     validate_strategy(strategy_row)
L00040:     validate_strategy(strategy_col)
L00041:     return calculate_payoffs(strategy_row, strategy_col)
L00042: 
L00043: def run_iterated_game(rounds, row_strategy_func, col_strategy_func):
L00044:     """Run iterated contest for given number of rounds with specified iterated strategy functions."""
L00045:     history = []
L00046:     for _ in range(rounds):
L00047:         next_move_row = row_strategy_func(history)
L00048:         next_move_col = col_strategy_func(history)
L00049:         history.append((next_move_row, next_move_col))
L00050:     return history
L00051: 
L00052: def compute_overall_scores(history):
L00053:     """Compute final scores for both sides."""
L00054:     result_game_payoffs = [game_payoffs(strat_profile[0], strat_profile[1]) for strat_profile in history]
L00055:     row_payoffs = [payoff_tupp[0] for payoff_tupp in result_game_payoffs]
L00056:     col_payoffs = [payoff_tupp[1] for payoff_tupp in result_game_payoffs]
L00057:     np_row_payoffs = np.asarray(row_payoffs, dtype=np.float32)
L00058:     np_col_payoffs = np.asarray(col_payoffs, dtype=np.float32)
L00059:     return np.mean(np_row_payoffs), np.mean(np_col_payoffs)
L00060: 
L00061: def simulation_mean_scores(row_strategy_func, col_strategy_func, num_rounds, num_simulations):
L00062:     """Run Monte-Carlo simulation, return mean score estimates."""
L00063:     row_scores = []
L00064:     col_scores = []
L00065:     for _ in range(num_simulations):
L00066:         final_history = run_iterated_game(num_rounds, row_strategy_func, col_strategy_func)
L00067:         row_score, col_score = compute_overall_scores(final_history)
L00068:         row_scores.append(row_score)
L00069:         col_scores.append(col_score)
L00070:     np_row_scores = np.asarray(row_scores, dtype=np.float32)
L00071:     np_col_scores = np.asarray(col_scores, dtype=np.float32)
L00072:     row_mean = np.mean(np_row_scores)
L00073:     col_mean = np.mean(np_col_scores)
L00074:     return row_mean, col_mean
L00075: 
L00076: def evaluate():
L00077:     row_score, _ = simulation_mean_scores(row_strategy, target_column_strategy, 10, 10000)
L00078:     metrics = {"Score": float(row_score)}
L00079:     print(json.dumps(metrics))
L00080:     
L00081: evaluate()
